definitions: A network virtualization technology that encapsulates Layer 2 Ethernet frames within Layer 3 UDP packets, allowing for the creation of large, scalable virtual networks over an existing IP infrastructure.
An overlay network technology used to extend Layer 2 segments across an IP network, often employed in data centers and cloud environments.
examples: Many modern data centers utilize VXLAN for network segmentation.
Configuring VXLAN tunnels is crucial for this deployment.
The performance benefits of VXLAN are significant.
